_comment: This project's inputs to the shared turn-loop hooks in claude-hub/hooks/.
The mechanism lives in the hub; every string specific to CNCBuild lives here.
Layered over hub defaults.json - `denies` merge by name and then FIELD BY FIELD, so the hub's
'push' rule applies here unchanged and is deliberately not restated.

source._extensions: The KiCad design files, plus the Python that can regenerate the schematic. Markdown is deliberately NOT source: this repo is mostly prose - build notes, commissioning measurements, design write-ups - and the only runnable check here is ERC/DRC, which has nothing to say about an edit to machine/README.md. Demanding it after a prose edit would only teach me to run it as a ritual, or to ignore the gate. Same call Simulator made about its own .md files.
source._ignore: Checked 2026-08-29, and empty on purpose. Nothing writes source into this repo during a turn except me: there is no .github/workflows directory at all, the repo ships no script that commits (grepped the tracked .py/.md/.html for `git add`/`git commit`/`subprocess` - zero hits; generate.py only writes the .kicad_sch), and no other project's tooling targets this repo - the conversation capture commits into claude-hub, not here. Add an entry when a writer appears whose paths intersect the list above, not before.

verify._note: A schematic that 'looks right' is not evidence - the whole point of committing the KiCad files is that a machine can check them. ERC catches the schematic errors (unconnected pins, conflicting drivers); DRC with --schematic-parity catches the board ones AND that the PCB still matches the schematic. The command sweeps every project under linear-encoder/kicad rather than naming one, so adding a third board needs no edit here. Either command satisfies the gate, because the mechanism sets 'verified' on the first pattern match - the checklist asks for both, and an edit that touched only one file honestly only needs its own. --exit-code-violations makes a violation a nonzero exit (5), so a failure cannot be mistaken for a pass. Known standing violation as of 2026-08-29: controller-board [invalid_outline], no edges on Edge.Cuts - the 67-68 x 20mm outline is settled in prose but not yet drawn. Expect it until it is; do not read it as your change breaking something. The sensor board has no .kicad_pcb at all yet, so DRC simply finds nothing there. The Where-Object filter is NOT decoration: VS Code's .history/ folder keeps whole copies of the KiCad files, git ignores them but Get-ChildItem does not, and without the filter the sweep silently checks stale snapshots twice over and reports their violations as yours.
verify.command: $k = 'C:\Program Files\KiCad\10.0\bin\kicad-cli.exe' ; $live = { $_.FullName -notmatch '\.history|-backups' } ; Get-ChildItem linear-encoder\kicad -Recurse -Filter *.kicad_sch | Where-Object $live | ForEach-Object { & $k sch erc --severity-error --exit-code-violations $_.FullName } ; Get-ChildItem linear-encoder\kicad -Recurse -Filter *.kicad_pcb | Where-Object $live | ForEach-Object { & $k pcb drc --schematic-parity --severity-error --exit-code-violations $_.FullName }
verify.label: KiCad ERC + DRC

checklist: == TURN LOOP (c:\github\claude-hub\playbooks\turn_workflow_loop.md - canonical, follow all of it) ==
1. PLAN FIRST. Before the first Edit/Write, state in your visible response what you understood and
how you intend to do it. A plain question ("can we...", "is X possible...") is a DISCUSSION -
answer it and stop. Record it:
c:\github\claude-hub\tools\turn.ps1 plan "<restated ask + approach>"
2. IMPLEMENT. One AskUserQuestion call at a time.
3. COMMIT AS YOU GO - each piece the moment it is verified. Never save commits up.
4. VERIFY, if the edit touched a KiCad file:
& 'C:\Program Files\KiCad\10.0\bin\kicad-cli.exe' sch erc --severity-error --exit-code-violations <sch>
& 'C:\Program Files\KiCad\10.0\bin\kicad-cli.exe' pcb drc --schematic-parity --severity-error --exit-code-violations <pcb>
5. HAND OFF - say plainly what is settled and what still needs a measurement off the machine.
THIS REPO'S SHAPE (README.md is canonical):
- THE MACHINE IS THE AUTHORITY, NOT THE CONFIGURATION. Anything in commissioning/ was measured;
anything quoted from a config file is labelled as such. $130 once read 889mm against a real
860mm because a catalog preset overwrote a measured value - and quietly cost soft-limit
protection until it was found by accident.
- DATASHEETS ARE COMMITTED, NOT LINKED. A link is not a copy: the ESP32 module's header pinout
was extracted once, lost, and had to be recovered from a schematic - and both vendor URLs
refuse a plain fetch.
- generate.py is a SEED, not live tooling. KiCad owns controller-board.kicad_sch now, and the
script still writes that absolute path - running it would overwrite hand edits. Do not run it
to 'refresh' anything without being asked.
- Ask before inventing a wiring or dimension detail. The user corrects iteratively and dislikes
invented specs; an unknown stays unknown until it is measured.
- The firmware (stevenrwood/iMXRT1062, branch srw/local-build-config) and ioSender itself live in
other repos. Work on either is a SEPARATE session there - one project per session, or the
conversation log files under the wrong project.
